editorial.tldr: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro surfaced after Arena testing on Oct 23 and launched Oct 24 as a multi-trillion-parameter flagship served via API. A botched launch forced a quota reset and apology, and third-party hosts started listing it within days.
editorial.whats_new: Huawei Ascend now supports LoRA fine-tuning of Kimi K3.1 Pro on a 128-card Atlas 950 SuperPoD, following Moore Threads day-zero serving support and the Nov 5 open-weights release.
editorial.why_it_matters: Open weights plus day-0 vLLM and non-NVIDIA accelerator support make Kimi K3.1 Pro a self-hostable and fine-tunable frontier-class option, though at roughly 1.56TB of weights it is a large-cluster deployment.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the weights license commercial-use conditions before planning self-hosting, budget for a large multi-GPU cluster given the 1.56TB checkpoint, and keep a fallback model since the hosted API had quota problems at launch.

status.detail: Weights are public with conditional commercial use, and inference and fine-tuning support is spreading across engines, clouds and domestic Chinese accelerators.
